anchor.statement: Lemma 7.4. For each sign σ , let t h σ = B(z + , z − ) T solve (t h σ ) ′ = A Φ t h σ − dth σ with z + (0) = P(0), z − (0) = 0. This specifies the real amplitude of the homogeneous m = 1 problem, with pressure given by (7.13) at f m = 0. With K a , N a , s a as in (7.7), write t h σ = x(e r − s a K a ) + yN a . Then cP(v) ≤ x(v) ≤ CP(v), y(v) x(v) = c 0 √︂ 1 + s(v)2 + O(S −1 ∗ ). (7.21) Every fixed derivative of this homogeneous solution in the coefficient variables or pulse coordinate is bounded by C I S b I ∗ P(v). Its homogeneous pressure, given by (7.13) with f = 0, has the extra factor ε 1/2 .

correspondence.by: Christian Garry (drafted with Claude Code; second review by ChatGPT, checked)
correspondence.note: Split into the bounds cP ≤ x ≤ CP and y/x = c0√(1 + s²) + O(S∗^{−1}) (the eigenvector is c0√(1 + s²) in primary_gaussian_bounds), the derivative bounds C_I S∗^{b_I} P, and the factor ε^{1/2} in the homogeneous pressure. Hypotheses are the coefficient estimates of Lemma 7.1 rather than the label phases.
